OriginalClaimStatement: ProvenanceX achieves 100% false-positive free detection of software supply-chain attacks across all attack vectors.
OperationalBoundary: Achieves 98.75% attack recall post-remediation (vs. 80.00% pre-remediation on Day 12). 0% false positives observed across evaluated 1,000 trials when in-tree generated path exemptions are declared. Detection requires active multi-layer evidence; out-of-boundary activity is undetectable.
DemonstratedFailureCondition: Demonstrated failure on ADV-HUNT-01 (filesystem modification outside monitored workspace root boundary), ADV-HUNT-03 (sub-10ms ephemeral process in user-mode), and ADV-HUNT-05 (dictionary-word subdomain tunneling).

OriginalClaimStatement: Sub-millisecond (12.4 µs) supply-chain attack detection latency with negligible runtime overhead.
OperationalBoundary: Pure in-memory cross-layer evidence correlation requires 12.4 µs (mean). However, end-to-end physical build overhead is 0.24% (~2.4 ms on standard compilation). Disk streaming hash verification on large artifacts (>100MB) incurs up to 48.2 ms.
DemonstratedFailureCondition: Equating pure algorithmic in-memory correlation speed with total end-to-end build wall-clock overhead is invalid. Disk I/O dominates physical artifact hashing.

OriginalClaimStatement: Linear or sub-linear O(1)/O(N) computational and memory scaling across arbitrary graph scales and dependency depths.
OperationalBoundary: Empirically validated up to 1,000 artifacts, 500 dependencies, and 10,000 evidence nodes. In-memory graph topological construction and validation scales linearly at 4.8 µs per node with peak memory <24 MB.
DemonstratedFailureCondition: Unbounded reachability queries without topological sort caching would exhibit O(V^3) latency on dense graphs.

OriginalClaimStatement: Guarantees acyclic evidence lineage DAG and uniquely localizes the root-cause layer of any supply-chain tampering.
OperationalBoundary: Strict DAG acyclicity verified across all 1,000 trials. Root cause isolation accurately pinpoints the lowest topological layer where evidence requirements fail.
DemonstratedFailureCondition: Simultaneous multi-layer tampering localizes the earliest topological violation rather than reporting all independent disjoint forks unless multi-root traversal is enabled.

OriginalClaimStatement: Detects all temporal ordering anomalies, causal inversions, and retroactive evidence modifications.
OperationalBoundary: Detects commit timestamp backdating, retroactive evidence modification, and out-of-order build stages within the resolution of host monotonic clocks.
DemonstratedFailureCondition: Sub-millisecond clock skew between distributed asynchronous CI runners cannot be distinguished from causal inversion without synchronized PTP/hardware timestamping.

OriginalClaimStatement: Comprehensive PE/ELF structural forensic detection of section entropy anomalies, header tampering, and debug signature stripping.
OperationalBoundary: Validates PE/COFF and ELF headers, section entropy (detecting packed/encrypted code >7.2 Shannon entropy), debug directory matching, and Authenticode/digital signatures.
DemonstratedFailureCondition: Low-entropy code injections or padding-manipulated polyglot payloads that mimic legitimate compiler section structures can evade static entropy thresholds.

OriginalClaimStatement: Deterministic, standalone evidence bundle verification with zero database and zero network dependencies.
OperationalBoundary: Air-gapped verification binary operates with zero network sockets and zero external dependencies. Cryptographically validates tar.gz archives, SHA-256 manifests, Ed25519/ECDSA/RSA signatures, and in-toto SLSA attestations.
DemonstratedFailureCondition: Verification cannot dynamically query online Certificate Revocation Lists (CRLs) or Rekor transparency logs without violating air-gapped isolation.

OriginalClaimStatement: Complete runtime observability of all build-time processes, filesystem modifications, and network connections.
OperationalBoundary: Complete 100% event capture is achieved only with Windows Administrator privileges via Kernel ETW providers. User-mode fallback relies on process polling and directory change notifications.
DemonstratedFailureCondition: In unprivileged user-mode CI runners, sub-10ms ephemeral processes (ADV-HUNT-03) and rapid create-and-delete transient file races (ADV-HUNT-04) evade capture.

OriginalClaimStatement: Guarantees 100% detection of unseen supply-chain attack vectors and multi-stage composed mutations.
OperationalBoundary: Evaluated across 11 unseen attack scenarios (5,500 trials) and 3 composed multi-layer attack scenarios (750 trials) with 100% recall on the evaluated suites.
DemonstratedFailureCondition: Does not generalize to attacks operating entirely outside configured workspace paths or low-entropy dictionary-word subdomain tunneling.

OriginalClaimStatement: Zero false positives across all software development workflows and real-world build systems.
OperationalBoundary: Zero false positives (0/1,000 trials, 100% specificity) observed on standard builds when legitimate in-tree generated files (e.g. mock_*.go, protobuf, swagger) are declared in policy.
DemonstratedFailureCondition: Default strict repository cleanliness policy triggers false positives if code generation tools write untracked files without declared path exemptions (BENIGN-HUNT-04).
